headline: KSE-100 sheds 825 points to 169,600 as Hormuz risk premium widens and IMF flags Gulf-linked revenue losses; Wall Street softens on a 5.28% 10-year yield while gold/silver rebound above $4,170/$61
mood: Risk-off persists · Hormuz premium and a hawkish Fed keep yields elevated

five_things.chip: KSE-100 Extends Losses on Hormuz Escalation
five_things.html: The KSE-100 opened firmly at 170,944.34 but selling accelerated after 2pm as reports that President Trump had rejected an Iranian ceasefire proposal on the Strait of Hormuz rattled sentiment, dragging the index to an intraday low of 169,538.22 and a close of 169,600.40, down 825.22 points (−0.48%). Volume rose to 568.04 million shares (from 421.01 million) on traded value of Rs20.81 billion, with decliners swamping advancers 305 to 154 (37 unchanged) across 496 names. Selling was broad-based across automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs, with heavyweights HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, PPL, PSO and HBL all trading lower; the government separately briefed the IMF that Gulf-conflict disruptions have caused revenue losses and slowed economic activity. Business Recorder and ARY News confirm the print.

five_things.chip: Wall Street Softens as Yields Hit Multi-Decade Highs
five_things.html: US equities drifted lower as the bond selloff continued: the S&P 500 slipped 0.17% to 7,671, the Dow fell 130.52 points (−0.25%) to 51,350, and the Nasdaq Composite eased 0.09% to 26,797. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed 4bps to 5.28% while the 30-year touched its highest since 2002 at 5.61%; the 2-year eased slightly to 4.89%. Losses were pared after New York Fed President John Williams suggested the central bank could hold until December before hiking again, even as CME FedWatch still prices 68% odds of an October move and 95% for December. CNBC and Investrade confirm the levels.

five_things.chip: Gold, Silver Rebound From Monday's Selloff
five_things.html: Bullion clawed back Monday's sharp losses as softer US labour-market and consumer-confidence data cooled October rate-hike bets: spot gold rose 1.42% to $4,172.40 an ounce and silver gained 1.23% to $61.27, both recovering from the prior session's 3%-plus slide. Kitco AM and Kitco PM report confirm the rebound.

five_things.chip: Oil Splits: Brent Holds Hormuz Premium, WTI Eases
five_things.html: Crude benchmarks diverged: Brent held near $105.31, barely changed on the session as the Strait of Hormuz risk premium persists, while WTI slid $3.22 (−3.48%) to $89.38 as Strategic Petroleum Reserve tapping and a partial easing of US-Iran rhetoric weighed on the domestic contract. Trading Economics and IEA confirm the spread.

five_things.chip: GCC: Saudi Non-Oil PMI Cools, OPEC+ Holds October Output
five_things.html: Saudi Arabia's non-oil private sector notched a 25th straight month of growth, but the PMI eased to 56.6 in September from 57.7 in August as output and new-order growth moderated from recent peaks. Separately, OPEC+'s seven core members (Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman) held October production at September levels, with Saudi output steady near 9.89mn bpd and the group's next meeting set for 4 October. Gulf News and IEA confirm the readings.

matrix.local_html: Pakistan's tape stayed on the back foot: the KSE-100 shed 0.48% to 169,600.40 as a fresh Hormuz escalation — Washington's rejection of an Iranian ceasefire proposal — drove broad selling across autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs, with breadth deeply negative (305 decliners vs 154 advancers). The government briefed the IMF that Gulf-conflict disruptions have already caused revenue losses and slowed activity, a headwind for the ongoing fourth EFF review. Domestically, the SBP held its policy rate at 11.5% for a third consecutive meeting on 14 September even as CPI inflation held in double digits at 11.15% YoY in August (from 9.20% in July), with 6-month KIBOR tracking near 12.6%, per Trading Economics. Today (30 September) is also the FBR's final, non-extended deadline for salaried individuals and AOPs to file Tax Year 2026 returns, with late filers facing a jump in penalties from Rs1,000 to Rs25,000 and loss of active-filer status from 1 October, per Business Recorder.
matrix.gcc_html: GCC markets stay anchored by a firm oil tape and a resilient, if decelerating, non-oil economy: Brent held near $105.31 on the Hormuz risk premium even as WTI eased on SPR tapping, while OPEC+'s seven core producers held October output at September levels (Saudi near 9.89mn bpd), with the next meeting set for 4 October, per IEA. Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI eased to 56.6 in September from 57.7 in August — still a 25th consecutive month of expansion but a step down from recent highs — per Gulf News. The PIF's 2026-2030 strategy, approved in April, continues to anchor Vision 2030 deployment across the Vision, Strategic and Financial portfolios.
matrix.global_html: Wall Street drifted lower as the bond selloff extended: the S&P 500 fell 0.17% to 7,671, the Dow lost 0.25% and the Nasdaq eased 0.09%, while the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.28% and the 30-year touched its highest since 2002 at 5.61%, per CNBC. Losses were cushioned after NY Fed President John Williams floated a December pause, though futures still price 68% odds of an October hike and 95% for December. On trade, new Section 338 tariff revisions and Canadian import restrictions took effect 29 September, while Congress's stopgap funding bill — passed in August — keeps federal agencies funded through 11 December, averting a shutdown at today's fiscal year-end, per NPR.

legislative.policy_html: FBR income tax return deadline — 30 September 2026 final date for salaried individuals/AOPs under Tax Year 2026 rules; no extension granted despite industry requests citing IRIS portal issues; late-filer category abolished from 1 October with penalties rising from Rs1,000 to Rs25,000
legislative.sectors: Salaried taxpayers, FBR/tax compliance, banking withholding
legislative.impact_html: Wins: FBR revenue documentation drive, early/compliant filers avoiding steep penalties. Loses: taxpayers facing IRIS portal delays; late filers hit with a 25x penalty jump and loss of active-filer status.

legislative.policy_html: OPEC+ output hold — seven core producers keep October production at September levels (Saudi ~9.89mn bpd); next OPEC+ meeting 4 October; Saudi non-oil PMI cools to 56.6 from 57.7
legislative.sectors: Energy, petrochemicals, Gulf non-oil private sector
legislative.impact_html: Wins: Gulf oil exporters and sovereign balance sheets from a firmer Brent floor near $105. Loses: oil-importing economies including Pakistan facing higher energy import bills; GCC non-oil momentum shows early signs of cooling.

legislative.policy_html: Stopgap funding bill (signed August) funds the federal government through 11 December 2026, averting a shutdown at today's fiscal year-end; new Section 338 tariff revisions and Canadian import restrictions took effect 29 September
legislative.sectors: Federal contractors & agencies, trade/industrials, rate-sensitive equities
legislative.impact_html: Wins: federal agencies and contractors gain funding certainty through mid-December. Loses: Canadian exporters facing new import restrictions; duration-sensitive equities as the Fed keeps a tightening bias alive with 10Y yields at multi-decade highs.

levels.support_note: psychological floor just below Tuesday's 169,538 intraday low; deeper support at 168,200
levels.resistance_note: Tuesday's opening high of 170,944; then 171,700 (Monday's intraday peak)

desk_stance_html: The desk reads Tuesday's action as a continuation of the external, oil-and-rates-driven risk-off move rather than a local growth story — the KSE-100's 0.48% decline came on broad but orderly selling, with the SBP's steady 11.5% policy rate still net-supportive of the local case even as the IMF flags Gulf-linked revenue pressure. The bigger swing factors into Wednesday remain external: a Hormuz-driven Brent premium near $105, a 10-year Treasury yield at 5.28% with the 30-year at its highest since 2002, and a Fed under Chair Warsh still leaning hawkish are keeping global risk appetite compressed, even as gold and silver's rebound shows some rotation back into havens. We'd watch 169,000 as first support (deeper at 168,200) and 170,900 as the level to reclaim before calling the pullback over, with 169,600 as the pivot. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.

Economic Vibes · Wednesday, 30 September 2026

THE OVERNIGHT TAPE
Wall Street drifted lower as the bond selloff extended: S&P 500 -0.17% to 7,671, Dow -0.25% to 51,350, Nasdaq -0.09% to 26,797. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.28% and the 30-year touched its highest level since 2002 at 5.61%. Losses were cushioned after NY Fed President John Williams floated a December pause, though futures still price 68% odds of an October hike and 95% for December. Gold (+1.42% to $4,172.40) and silver (+1.23% to $61.27) rebounded from Monday's selloff.

PAKISTAN
The KSE-100 fell 0.48% (-825.22 pts) to 169,600.40 as reports that Washington rejected an Iranian ceasefire proposal on the Strait of Hormuz drove broad-based selling across autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, E&P and OMCs. Breadth was deeply negative: 305 decliners vs 154 advancers. The government briefed the IMF that Gulf-conflict disruptions have already caused revenue losses and slowed economic activity. SBP holds its policy rate at 11.5% for a third straight meeting; CPI stayed in double digits at 11.15% YoY in August. Today is also the FBR's final tax return deadline for salaried individuals — no extension granted, penalties jumping to Rs25,000.

GCC
Brent held near $105.31 on the Hormuz premium while WTI eased 3.48% to $89.38 on SPR tapping. OPEC+'s seven core producers held October output at September levels, with Saudi near 9.89mn bpd and the next meeting set for 4 October. Saudi Arabia's non-oil PMI cooled to 56.6 from 57.7 — still a 25th straight month of growth, but decelerating.

GLOBAL
New Section 338 tariff revisions and Canadian import restrictions took effect 29 September. Congress's August stopgap funding bill keeps federal agencies funded through 11 December, averting a shutdown at today's fiscal year-end — but the fiscal cliff is deferred, not resolved.

LEGISLATIVE TRACKER
• Pakistan: FBR tax deadline today — wins: compliant filers, revenue documentation. Loses: IRIS-delayed and late filers facing a 25x penalty jump.
• GCC: OPEC+ output hold — wins: Gulf oil exporters on a firmer Brent floor. Loses: oil-importing economies including Pakistan.
• Global: US funding bill through 11 Dec — wins: federal contractors. Loses: Canadian exporters, duration-sensitive equities.

THE DAY AHEAD
KSE-100 support 169,000 (deeper at 168,200) · pivot 169,600 (Tuesday's close) · resistance 170,900 (Tuesday's open), then 171,700. The desk reads this as an external, oil-and-rates-driven risk-off move rather than a local growth story. All levels are indicative desk estimates, not recommendations.
